text.p: All hostages were released by prisoners and five people were reported killed as a rebellion ended on Thursday at Latin America's largest jail here, a police spokesman said.

Prisoners took 27 hostages at Sao Paulo's Carandiru jail on Wednesday, demanding to be transferred to another prison, while others hijacked a garbage truck and tried to escape by ramming the prison gates.
Four prisoners and one prison worker were killed in the attempted jailbreak.

The police spokesman said all hostages had been released in exchange for being transferred to another jail in Sao Paulo state. "Everything is under control now; all hostages have been released and the prisoners have been transferred."

With some 6,300 inmates and more than 1,000 guards and administrative staff, Carandiru is Latin America's largest prison complex. In May, 53 inmates escaped from there after digging a tunnel under the prison walls. Carandiru is also the site of Brazil's most violent riot, in which 111 inmates were shot and killed by military police in October 1992.
